title: Conormal intersection for a locally Koszul-regular quotient ideal
statement: Let $T$ be a commutative ring, let $L\subseteq K$ be ideals of $T$, and put $\overline T=T/L$ and $\overline K=K/L\subseteq\overline T$. Assume that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset\overline T$ containing $\overline K$, there exist $h\in\overline T\setminus\mathfrak p$, an integer $r\geq0$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in\overline T_h$ such that $$\overline K\,\overline T_h=(f_1,\ldots,f_r),\qquad H_i(K_\bullet(\overline T_h;f_1,\ldots,f_r))=0\quad(i>0).$$ Localization at $h$ uses [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and the displayed homology vanishing is Koszul regularity [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Then $$L\cap K^2=LK.$$ The powers and product are ideal products. No Noetherian, locality or flatness hypothesis on $T$ is imposed, and the sequence may be empty.

source.place: Tag 07CX (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular-ideal), specialized to a Koszul-regular quotient ideal; vanishing of all positive Koszul homology includes vanishing of H_1. The local ideal condition is spelled out as in definition-regular-ideal.

proof.text: The inclusion $LK\subseteq L\cap K^2$ follows term by term from $L\subseteq K$: a product $lk$ belongs to $L$ and to $K^2$. For the reverse inclusion fix $x\in L\cap K^2$. For an ideal $H\subseteq T$ and a localization $S$ of $T$, write $HS$ for the ideal generated by the images of $H$. We will show $x/1\in(LK)T_{\mathfrak m}$ for each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $T$.

source.place: Tag 07CX (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular-ideal), proof by localization from Tag 0666 (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular)

proof.text: If $K\not\subseteq\mathfrak m$, choose $k\in K\setminus\mathfrak m$. Since $x\in L$, the product $xk$ belongs to $LK$, and $x/1=(xk)/k$ in $T_{\mathfrak m}$. Thus $x/1\in(LK)T_{\mathfrak m}$. No regularity hypothesis is used in this case.

source.place: Tag 07CX (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular-ideal), proof by localization from Tag 0666 (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular)

proof.text: Now suppose $K\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Since $L\subseteq\mathfrak m$, the image $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m/L$ is a prime of $T/L$ containing $K/L$: membership of the class of $a$ is precisely $a\in\mathfrak m$, so primality follows from that of $\mathfrak m$. Choose $h,r,f_1,\ldots,f_r$ from the hypothesis at $\mathfrak p$, and lift $h$ to $t\in T\setminus\mathfrak m$. Put $A=T_t$, $I=LA$ and $J=KA$. The quotient-localization isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] identifies $A/I$ with $(T/L)_h$ by $a/t^n\mapsto\bar a/h^n$, and identifies $J/I$ with $(K/L)(T/L)_h$. In this identified ring the given $f_i$ generate $J/I$. Choose preimages $g_i\in J$ under $J\to J/I$. The given homology vanishing includes $H_1=0$, exactly the definition of an $H_1$-regular sequence in [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Thus the images of the $g_i$ have the global generation and $H_1$-regularity needed in the next step.

source.place: Tag 07CX (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular-ideal), proof by localization from Tag 0666 (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-h1-regular-quotient-ideal-intersection] to the commutative ring $A$, the ideals $I\subseteq J$, and these $g_i$. It gives $I\cap J^2=IJ$. Since $x\in L\cap K^2$, its image belongs to $I\cap J^2$, hence to $IJ=(LK)A$. For the last equality, both ideals are generated by the products $(l/1)(k/1)=(lk)/1$ with $l\in L$ and $k\in K$; expanding finite sums in the extended ideals proves both inclusions. The same argument applies to $r=0$, when the list of lifts is empty.

source.place: Tag 07CX (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular-ideal), proof by localization from Tag 0666 (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular)

proof.text: Write the membership $x/1\in(LK)T_t$ as a finite sum $x/1=\sum_j (a_j/t^{n_j})(b_j/1)$ with $b_j\in LK$. Choose $N\geq n_j$ for all $j$ and set $b=\sum_j t^{N-n_j}a_jb_j\in LK$. Then $x/1=b/t^N$. The fraction equality in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives $t^q(t^Nx-b)=0$ for some $q\geq0$, hence $t^{N+q}x=t^qb\in LK$. Since $t\notin\mathfrak m$, we have $x/1=(t^{N+q}x)/t^{N+q}\in(LK)T_{\mathfrak m}$. The zero finite sum is covered by $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), equality of fractions; the denominator computation makes explicit the localization step in more-algebra.tex Tag 07CX

proof.text: The two cases prove $x/1\in(LK)T_{\mathfrak m}$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-membership-at-maximal-localizations] with ideal $LK$ to conclude $x\in LK$. Since $x\in L\cap K^2$ was arbitrary, this is the reverse inclusion and proves the equality. The zero ring is included: it has no maximal ideals and the same cited membership criterion applies.

source.place: Tag 00HN, local detection of zero elements, applied to T/(LK); completes the localization argument in more-algebra.tex Tag 07CX

The item statement is unchanged from live; only status, proof, proof_deps, split_report and searches changed. It is a faithful Koszul-regular specialization of 07CX, and Koszul-regular implies H_1-regular directly by the definitions in def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence. The delivery adds no new nodes. Steps 1-2 are elementary: LK is contained in L∩K², and if K is not inside m then x/1=xk/k. Step 3: m/L is a prime of T/L containing K/L, and the lift t lies outside m. lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute (B=T, J=L, b=t) gives the identification with the right formula, and the Koszul H_1 vanishing carries over through the ring isomorphism. Step 4 applies the same-unit lem-sfb-h1-regular-quotient-ideal-intersection (0666) with matching hypotheses, and (LA)(KA)=(LK)A by expanding generators. Step 5 writes out the denominator clearing: t^q(t^N x-b)=0 gives t^{N+q}x in LK, so E5 does not apply. Step 6 is Ideal.mem_of_localization_maximal. Edge cases L=T, K=L (empty sequence), T=0 and k[x,y] with L=(x), K=(x,y) all agree. A DAG grep for 07CX/0666 found no duplicate; lem-weil-pbc-conormal-intersection-regular-quotient needs a global regular sequence, which is stronger. The only cited non-leaf statement is in the item's own unit, so no tool_uses entry is needed. No SGA, no cycle, no repair note.
